h1: Off-peak hot water fails, but boost works
title: Off-peak hot water fails, but boost works | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand off-peak hot water fails, but boost works. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Working boost with failed off-peak heating can indicate separate supplies, controls or heater paths; it does not prove the whole cylinder has failed.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: The Electromax manufacturer fault diagrams distinguish off-peak and boost immersion paths. Other direct-cylinder systems also need their actual wiring and programme arrangement identified, rather than assuming they match that model.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Record the tariff arrangement, normal schedule and which accessible control produces hot water. Internal supply checks and electrical testing must be carried out by a suitably competent person.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: What does working boost tell us about a failed off-peak programme?
faqs.answer: It shows one heating path may still operate; timed supply, controls and the other heater path require separate competent investigation.
